issue.title: rpc: invalidateblock reports success when a block can't be disconnected
issue.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Current behaviour

If `Chainstate::InvalidateBlock` fails part way through, the `invalidateblock` RPC still returns `null` as if it succeeded.

The RPC helper ignores the return value of `InvalidateBlock` and only throws when `state` is invalid ([src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L1765-L1773](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/649bc0a645eb127a9b1e6d078f8d129be6380c87/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L1765-L1773)):

```cpp
chainman.ActiveChainstate().InvalidateBlock(state, pblockindex);

if (state.IsValid()) {
    chainman.ActiveChainstate().ActivateBestChain(state);
}

if (!state.IsValid()) {
    throw JSONRPCError(RPC_DATABASE_ERROR, state.ToString());
}
```

`DisconnectTip` returns `false` without touching `state` when `DisconnectBlock` fails, for example when `ReadBlockUndo` hits a checksum mismatch or a missing `rev*.dat` file ([src/validation.cpp#L2956-L2959](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/649bc0a645eb127a9b1e6d078f8d129be6380c87/src/validation.cpp#L2956-L2959)). `InvalidateBlock` then returns `false` from inside its disconnect loop ([src/validation.cpp#L3591-L3594](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/649bc0a645eb127a9b1e6d078f8d129be6380c87/src/validation.cpp#L3591-L3594)).

When that happens:

- every block above the failing one has already been disconnected and marked `BLOCK_FAILED_VALID`
- the tip is left at the block whose undo data couldn't be read
- the block passed to `invalidateblock` is not marked invalid
- the RPC returns `null`, and the only trace is a `DisconnectBlock ... failed` line in `debug.log`

The same silent success happens for the genesis block, where `InvalidateBlock` returns `false` early with a valid `state` ([src/validation.cpp#L3536-L3537](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/649bc0a645eb127a9b1e6d078f8d129be6380c87/src/validation.cpp#L3536-L3537)).

The same `DisconnectTip` failure during a normal reorg is fatal: `ActivateBestChainStep` aborts the node with "Failed to disconnect block" (#15305). Through `invalidateblock`, the user is told it worked.

### How I ran into this

I run a mainnet Bitcoin node. The mempool.space backend running against it kept failing with "Undo data expected but can't be read", and `bitcoind` logged `ReadBlockUndo: Checksum mismatch` for `rev05123.dat` every few seconds. `getblockstats` failed for six consecutive blocks, 913132 to 913137. Their undo records had been written in September 2025, and 576 KiB of the file in the middle of them had been replaced with zeros, most likely a lost write after an unclean shutdown.

A full `-reindex` would have taken days, so I looked at `invalidateblock 913132` followed by `reconsiderblock` as a shortcut. Reading the code showed it couldn't work. The rollback would disconnect about 58,400 blocks, stop at 913137 because that block's undo data can't be read, and then return `null`. Even if it had got through, `reconsiderblock` wouldn't have repaired anything, because `WriteBlockUndo` skips blocks that already have an undo position. I didn't run it.

I repaired the node another way, by rebuilding the six undo records from `-txindex` and writing them back in place. But nothing in the RPC's response would have told me the rollback stopped part way, which is why I'm filing this.

### Expected behaviour

`invalidateblock` returns an error when the requested block was not invalidated. The error should say that the rollback stopped early and at which block, so the user knows the chain is partly rolled back. For the genesis block, it should return a clear "cannot invalidate genesis block" error.

### Steps to reproduce

I found this by reading the code and haven't run these steps against master yet. On regtest:

1. Start a node and mine 10 blocks with `generatetoaddress`. Each block contains only a coinbase transaction.
2. Stop the node. Corrupt the undo record for block 5 by flipping one byte of its checksum in `blocks/rev00000.dat`. Each coinbase-only undo record is 41 bytes: 4 magic, 4 size, 1 byte for the empty `CBlockUndo`, and a 32-byte checksum. Genesis has no undo record, so block 5's checksum ends at offset `(5 - 1) * 41 + 40 = 204`.
3. Start the node and run `invalidateblock <hash of block 3>`.

From the code paths above, the RPC returns `null`, `getblockcount` returns 5, `getchaintips` does not show block 3 as invalid, and `debug.log` gets a `DisconnectTip(): DisconnectBlock <hash> failed` line. `invalidateblock <genesis hash>` also returns `null`.

### Relevant log output

From the mainnet node, repeated every few seconds while the mempool.space backend retried:

```
[error] ReadBlockUndo: Checksum mismatch at FlatFilePos(nFile=5123, nPos=1035211)
```

### How did you obtain Bitcoin Core

Not applicable, found by reading the source

### What version of Bitcoin Core are you using?

Not applicable. The code references above are from master at 649bc0a645eb127a9b1e6d078f8d129be6380c87.

### Operating system and version

Not relevant
